title.zh: 没有专利的发现，和一克镭的账
title.en: No Patents, and the Bill for a Gram of Radium

dek.zh: 居里夫妇把制备镭的方法毫无保留地公开，镭工业因此自由发展；他们自己却长期缺钱、缺场地。1921年赠镭之前，后来为本书写引言的梅洛尼去探访时，她的实验室仍设备不足；靠美国妇女募捐，居里夫人才得到一克镭。这是一笔两边都有分量的账。
dek.en: The Curies published their method for preparing radium without reserve, and the radium industry grew freely on it. They themselves long went without money and without a proper workplace. When Meloney, who later wrote the book's introduction, visited before the 1921 gift, Marie Curie's laboratory still lacked sufficient equipment, and a subscription raised by American women finally put a gram in Marie Curie's hands. It is a ledger with weight on both sides.

paras.zh: 1921年5月20日，白宫。美国妇女把一克镭赠给它的发现者，可镭本身并不在现场。哈定总统交给居里夫人的是一把小金钥匙，用来打开运送镭的箱子。装镭的管子还在“局”里，那里的官员主动提出代为测量、装箱并送上船。
paras.en: May 20, 1921, the White House. The women of America gave a gram of radium to its discoverer, but the radium itself was not in the room. What President Harding placed in Marie Curie's hands was a small golden key, the one that opened the casket devised for transporting the radium. The tubes of radium were still at the Bureau, whose officials had kindly offered to make the measurements and to take care of the packing and delivery to the ship.

paras.zh: 一克镭的市价是十万美元。而制备镭的方法，是她和丈夫皮埃尔·居里多年前毫无保留地公开的，镭工业正靠它发展起来、高价卖货。公开了方法的她，实验室里那点镭当时只用于为医院提取射气；后来为本书写引言的梅洛尼在美国发起募捐，希望借此让她把研究继续下去。这笔账书里两边都有记载：梅洛尼在引言里记下了市价和募捐，居里夫人自己在自传笔记里算过放弃的那笔财富。
paras.en: A gram of radium then sold for one hundred thousand dollars. The process for preparing it had been published years earlier, without reserve, by Marie Curie and her husband Pierre Curie, and the radium industry was now thriving on that very process and selling its product at a high price. She had helped give the method away, yet the radium in her laboratory was used at that time only for extracting emanations for hospital use, and Meloney, who later wrote the book's introduction, set out to raise a subscription in America to enable her to go on with her work. The book records both sides of that account: Meloney's introduction notes the price and the subscription, and in her autobiographical notes Marie Curie reckons up the fortune she gave up.

paras.zh: 事情要从1890年代末的巴黎说起。居里夫妇要从矿石里提取镭和钋，可他们缺合适的工作场所、缺人手，也缺钱。沥青铀矿很贵，他们买不起足够的量。当时这种矿物的主要来源在波希米亚的圣约阿希姆斯塔尔，奥地利政府在那里经营一座提铀的矿。矿上的残渣还从没用过，他们相信镭和一部分钋就在残渣里。靠维也纳科学院的影响，他们以优惠价拿到几吨残渣。起初的费用出自自己的积蓄，后来才得到少量补助和一些外部帮助。
paras.en: The story begins in Paris in the late 1890s. The Curies were trying to extract radium and polonium from ore, and they lacked a proper place to work in, personnel and money. Pitchblende was an expensive mineral, and they could not afford to buy a sufficient quantity. At that time the principal source of this mineral was at St. Joachimsthal in Bohemia, where the Austrian government worked a mine for the extraction of uranium. Its residues had so far not been used at all, and they believed the radium, and part of the polonium, would be found in them. Through the influence of the Vienna Academy of Sciences they secured several tons of the residues at an advantageous price. In the beginning the costs came out of their own pockets; only later were they given a few subventions and some help from outside sources.

paras.zh: 化学处理只能在一间废弃的储藏室里做：木棚、沥青地面、玻璃屋顶挡不住雨，里面没有任何设施，只有几张破松木桌、一个不好使的铸铁炉和皮埃尔爱用的黑板。没有排气罩带走化学处理放出的毒气，活儿得搬到院子里做；天气不好的时候就在棚里接着干，把窗子开着。
paras.en: The chemical treatments had to be carried on in an abandoned storeroom: a wooden shed with a bituminous floor and a glass roof that did not keep the rain out, and without any interior arrangements. All it contained were some worn pine tables, a cast-iron stove that worked badly, and the blackboard Pierre Curie loved to use. There were no hoods to carry away the poisonous gases thrown off by the treatments, so the work had to be moved outside into the court; when the weather was unfavorable they went on inside, leaving the windows open.

paras.zh: 这两年他们几乎无人相助。这里要补一句：实验室杂工珀蒂常在能挤出的时间里搭手；1898年，学校的实验室主任之一贝蒙临时帮过忙；1900年前后，青年化学家德比埃尔纳加入。分工后皮埃尔研究镭的性质，她负责把镭提纯成纯盐。她一次处理多达二十公斤材料，棚里堆满沉淀物和液体；她要搬运容器、转移液体，再用铁棒连续几小时搅拌铸铁锅里沸腾的物料。
paras.en: For two years they worked there practically unaided. One qualification: the laboratory helper, Petit, kept lending a hand in whatever time he could spare; G. Bemont, one of the laboratory chiefs at the School, gave temporary help in 1898; and around 1900 the young chemist André Debierne joined them. Once the work was divided, Pierre studied the properties of radium while Marie Curie pushed ahead with the chemical experiments aimed at preparing pure radium salts. She worked with as much as twenty kilogrammes of material at a time, until the hangar was full of great vessels of precipitates and liquids: moving the containers about, transferring the liquids, and stirring the boiling material in the cast-iron basin with an iron bar, for hours at a stretch.

paras.zh: 后来有一次（书中未写年份），日内瓦方面来请皮埃尔：那里物质条件更好，还能过上近似乡居的宁静生活。按居里夫人的记述，这个决定很艰难，皮埃尔动了心。最后让他定下来不去的，是他们正对镭做的研究，他怕这样的变动打断它。此时，索邦为医科学生而设的P.C.N.物理教席正好空缺。他申请后，在一心想让他不必离开法国的庞加莱的影响下获聘；她则受托在塞夫尔的女子师范学校讲物理课。他们留在巴黎，收入增加了，工作却更难：皮埃尔要兼两处课，其中学生众多的P.C.N.教学让他非常疲惫。
paras.en: At one point (the book gives no year), Geneva came calling for Pierre, offering material advantages and the opportunity of a life comparable in its tranquillity with that in the country. In Marie Curie's account the decision was a grave one, and Pierre was tempted. What finally settled it was the radium research itself, since he feared the interruption that such a change must involve. At this moment the chair of physics in the Sorbonne's P.C.N. course was vacant; this was the physics, chemistry and natural history curriculum compulsory for medical students. He applied, and was appointed through the influence of Henri Poincaré, who was anxious to free him from the necessity of quitting France. Marie Curie was given charge of the physics lectures at the Normal School for Girls at Sèvres. They stayed in Paris and their income increased, but working conditions grew harder: Pierre was doing double teaching, and the P.C.N., with its very large number of students, fatigued him greatly.

paras.zh: 新职位不带实验室。在索邦设于居维叶街12号、供P.C.N.教学用的附属楼里，他只有一间小办公室和一个工作间。他想接收学生做研究，就去争取更大的场地。照她的说法，做过这类事的人知道那是一堵怎样的墙：公文、登门、请求，有一点成果都要付出很多，这些事彻底让他厌倦和沮丧。除了这些困难，没有工业手段处理原料，研究也推不动。早在1899年，皮埃尔就借中央化学产品公司（他因制造天平与之有往来）的一处现成设施，组织了第一次工业试验，技术细节由德比埃尔纳安排得很成功，试验效果良好；这种需要特殊小心的活儿，还得专门训练人手。
paras.en: The new post came without a laboratory. In the annex of the Sorbonne at 12 rue Cuvier, which served as teaching quarters for the P.C.N., all he had at his disposition was a little office and a single work room. He meant to receive students and start them in research, so he took steps to find larger working quarters. Anyone who has taken similar steps knows the wall of financial and administrative obstacles he was throwing himself against: the official letters, the visits, the requests, and what even the least success entailed. It all thoroughly wearied and discouraged him. Besides these difficulties, the research could not advance without industrial means of treating the raw material. As early as 1899 Pierre Curie organized a first industrial experiment, using for it a chance installation placed at his disposition by the Central Society of Chemical Products, with which he had dealt over the construction of his balances. The technical details were arranged very successfully by André Debierne, and the operations brought good results, though a special crew had to be trained for chemical work that demanded special precautions.

paras.zh: 还有一件事，她在书里两处都写到。按她的叙述，在她同意之下，皮埃尔·居里拒绝从发现中获取任何物质利益，英译此处作「took no copyright」。他们把研究结果和制备镭的确切方法毫无保留地发表，来问的人也都得到答复。自传笔记里她又说了一遍：夫妇二人一贯不从发现中获取物质利益，方法从一开始就全部公开，没有申请专利，也不在工业开发中保留任何好处，此处英译作「took out no patent」。书里没写这个决定的日期。
paras.en: There is something else she writes about in two places in the book. In Marie Curie's telling, and with her agreement, Pierre Curie refused to draw any material profit from the discovery. As the English translation of the biography puts it, "We took no copyright": they published without reserve all the results of their research as well as the exact processes of the preparation of radium, and gave whatever information was asked of them. In the autobiographical notes she says it again: the two of them always refused to draw any material profit from the discovery, the process was published from the beginning, and they took out no patent and reserved no advantage in any industrial exploitation. The book gives no date for the decision.

paras.zh: 钱还是不够。受这次试验启发，法国实业家阿尔梅·德·利尔办起一座在当时看来很大胆的真正镭工厂，把产品卖给医生；医生们因各种研究的发表，已对镭的生物效应和可能的疗法产生兴趣。项目成功了，因为他能雇到居里夫妇训练过的人。镭从此有了稳定货源，价格很高：制备条件特殊，制镭所需矿物的价格又立刻上涨。德·利尔出于好意，在厂里给他们一小块工作地方和一部分费用。其余的钱有的是他们自己的，有的来自补助，最重要的一笔是1902年科学院给的20,000法郎。
paras.en: The money was still short. Inspired by their attempt, a French industrialist, Armet de Lisle, took what seemed at that epoch the daring step of founding a veritable radium factory to furnish the product to physicians, whose interest in the biological effects of radium and its possible therapeutic applications had been aroused by the publication of various investigations. The project proved a success because he could employ men already trained by the Curies in the delicate processes of the manufacture. Radium was now regularly placed on sale, at a high price it is true, given the special conditions under which it had to be made and the immediate rise in the cost of the minerals necessary to its production. Armet de Lisle, in an entirely disinterested manner, placed a little working place in his factory at their disposition, together with a part of the means necessary to use it. Other funds were added either by the Curies themselves or through subventions, the most important of which, accorded by the Academy of Sciences in 1902, amounted to 20,000 francs.

paras.zh: 1902年，她从矿渣里制得十分之一克纯氯化镭，只呈现新元素镭的谱线，并第一次测定这种元素的原子量，数值远高于钡，镭的化学个体性就此确立。1907年她做了更精确的第二次测定，定为225.35——她写书时公认的数值是226；她还和德比埃尔纳把镭制成了金属态。她亲手从矿石里提取的镭，按皮埃尔的意愿全部给了实验室，总量超过一克元素镭。
paras.en: In 1902 Marie Curie succeeded in preparing a decigramme of chloride of pure radium that gave only the spectrum of the new element, radium, and made a first determination of its atomic weight, a value much higher than that of barium. The chemical individuality of radium was completely established. In 1907 she made a second and more precise determination, as 225.35; the number accepted when she wrote was 226. She also succeeded, jointly with André Debierne, in obtaining radium in the state of metal. The total quantity she prepared and gave to the laboratory, in agreement with Pierre Curie's desire, amounted to more than a gramme of radium element.

paras.zh: 多年后，她在自传笔记里把账摊开。镭在矿石里含量极小，价格很高；镭又能治好多种疾病，所以制造利润很大。他们放弃的，是一笔本可留给子女的财富。更值得考虑的是许多朋友的反对：若当初保住权利，本可筹钱建一所像样的镭研究所，不必经历那些一直拖累两人、至今仍拖累她的难处。她承认朋友们的看法并非没有道理（英译作「not without reason」），但仍然认为他们做得对。
paras.en: Years later, in the autobiographical notes, she laid out the rest of the ledger. Radium is found in minerals in very small quantities, so its price is very high, and the profits of its manufacture have been great, since the substance is used to cure a number of diseases. What they sacrificed in renouncing the exploitation of their discovery, then, was a fortune, one that could after them have gone to their children. And what was even more to be considered, she wrote, was the objection of many of their friends, who argued "not without reason" that if they had guaranteed their rights they could have had the financial means of founding a satisfactory Institute of Radium, without the difficulties that had been such a handicap to both of them and were still a handicap to her. She conceded the point and held her ground all the same: "Yet, I still believe that we have done right."

paras.zh: 梅洛尼（本书引言作者）曾在纽约发起这次募捐。她见到居里夫人时，居里夫人说美国约有五十克镭，巴尔的摩四克、丹佛六克、纽约七克；在法国，她的实验室的镭几乎不超过一克。梅洛尼惊问她只有一克吗，她纠正说，那不是她的，而是属于她的实验室。梅洛尼那一周得知，一克镭市价十万美元。她的实验室虽然几乎是新楼，设备并不够用，那里的镭当时只用于为医院提取射气治疗癌症。梅洛尼原想几周后到纽约时，找十位女士各出一万美元买下一克，免去公开募捐的声势，结果只找到一两位。后来是十万名妇女和一批男士下决心要把钱募齐，不到一年基金就募成了。据居里夫人自己的记述，一个由几位知名女士和杰出科学家组成的委员会收到一些重要捐赠，并发起公众认捐，许多妇女组织、尤其是大学和俱乐部纷纷响应，不少捐款来自受益于镭疗法的人。就这样，集成了超过十万美元的居里夫人镭基金。
paras.en: Meloney, who later wrote the book's introduction, had launched the subscription in New York. When Meloney met her, Marie Curie said that America had about fifty grammes of radium: four of these in Baltimore, six in Denver, seven in New York, and on she went, naming the location of every grain. And in France? "My laboratory," she said, "has hardly more than a gramme." Meloney, astonished, exclaimed that she had only a gramme. "I? Oh, I have none," Marie Curie corrected. "It belongs to my laboratory." That week Meloney learned that the market price of a gramme of radium was one hundred thousand dollars. She also learned that Marie Curie's laboratory, although practically a new building, was without sufficient equipment, and that the radium held there was used at that time only for extracting emanations for hospital use in cancer treatment. When she arrived in New York a few weeks afterwards, Meloney had hoped to find ten women to subscribe ten thousand dollars each and buy a gramme without the publicity of a general campaign. She found one or two. There were not ten women to buy that gramme of radium, but there were a hundred thousand women and a group of men determined that the money must be raised, and in less than a year the fund had been raised. In Marie Curie's own account, a committee including several prominent women and distinguished scientific men received some important gifts and made an appeal for a public subscription. A great number of women's organizations, especially colleges and clubs, responded, and in many cases gifts came from persons who had experienced the benefit of radiumtherapy. In this way the "Marie Curie Radium Fund" of more than one hundred thousand dollars was collected.

paras.zh: 据梅洛尼记述，仪式前一夜又出了岔子：文件要把这一克镭放在居里夫人个人名下。她读完说不行。这一克镭代表很多钱，可它更代表美国的妇女，不是给她的，是给科学的。她身体不好，随时可能死；女儿伊夫尚未成年，一旦她去世，镭就会进她的遗产，由两个女儿分掉。她要求当晚就把文件办好：第二天就要接收镭，而她可能明天就死，事关重大（据梅洛尼转述）。于是那个闷热的五月夜晚，虽然已经很晚，他们还是请到律师，照她自拟的草稿写好文件。她在动身去华盛顿前签了字：她死后，这一克镭归巴黎的镭研究所，供居里实验室专用。第二天在白宫，哈定总统交给她的是一把小金钥匙。
paras.en: As Meloney tells it, on the eve of the ceremony there was one more snag: the papers were to put this gramme of radium in Marie Curie's own name. Marie Curie read them and said it must not be left that way. The gramme represented a great deal of money, but more than that it represented the women of the country: it was not for her, it was for science. She was not well and might die any day. Her daughter Eve was not of legal age, and if she died the radium would go into her estate and be divided between her daughters. That was not its purpose; it had to be consecrated for all time to the use of science. The paper had to be fixed that night, because the next day she received the radium, and, she said, as Meloney reports it, "I might die tomorrow. Too much is at stake." So, late as it was on that hot May evening, a lawyer was secured and prepared the paper from a draft Marie Curie herself had written. She signed it before starting for Washington: in the event of her death the gramme of radium went to the Institut du Radium in Paris, for the exclusive use of the Laboratoire Curie. The next day at the White House, what she received from President Harding was the small golden key.

paras.zh: 作者推断，这套选择的代价不是一次性的损失，而是一条链。方法公开后，工业自由发展，医生和科学家很快拿到了产品；同时矿物涨价，镭价居高不下。她的实验室设备不足，那里的镭当时只用于为医院提取射气；她亲手制得的一克多镭，全都给了实验室。一种解释是，他们用自己后来的研究条件，替整个行业垫了启动成本。
paras.en: The author's reading is that the cost of these choices was not a single loss but a chain. The method went public; the industry developed freely; physicians and scientists got their products quickly. At the same time the minerals got dearer and the price of radium stayed high. Her laboratory was without sufficient equipment, and the radium held there was used at that time only for extracting emanations for hospital use; the gramme and more that Marie Curie prepared with her own hands had gone entirely to the laboratory. One way to put it: they paid the start-up costs of a whole industry out of their own research conditions.

paras.zh: 她在自传笔记里给出了自己的说法（这是她的主张，不是可核对的事实）。人类需要实干者，他们为自身利益好好做事，同时不忘公共利益；人类也需要做梦者，他们一门心思追随目标，顾不上自己的物质好处。也许有人会说，这些理想主义者既然不想要财富，也就不配得到财富。但她认为，组织良好的社会应当给这样的工作者以高效工作的条件，让他们的生活没有物质之忧，可以专心服务科学研究。
paras.en: She gave her own account of it in the autobiographical notes, and it is her position, not a fact that can be checked: humanity needs practical men who make the best of their work for the sake of their own interests without forgetting the general interest, but it also needs dreamers, for whom the unselfish following of a purpose is so imperative that it becomes impossible for them to devote much attention to their own material benefit. No doubt it could be said that these idealists do not deserve riches, since they do not have the desire for them. A society well organized, she thought, ought to assure to these workers the means for efficient labor, in a life from which material care is excluded, so that the life may be freely devoted to the service of scientific research.

paras.zh: 作者提出另一种做法（书中没有写他们讨论过任何替代方案）：分用途授权，研究与教学免费，商业开发收费；或者只对产品收费，把方法留在公共领域。这条路或许能留下一点收入，代价是谈判、监督，以及与工业界的长期纠缠。朋友们主张的则是保留权利、用收益建研究所。作者认为，差别不在谁更高尚，而在谁承担风险。
paras.en: The author's alternative, and the book records no such discussion: license by use, free for research and teaching and charged for commercial exploitation, or else charge for the product and leave the method in the public domain. Some income might have been kept that way, at the price of negotiation, oversight, and a long entanglement with industry. What the friends urged was retaining the rights and building the institute out of the proceeds. In the author's view, the difference is not who is nobler; it is who carries the risk.

paras.zh: 今天常见的一幕：一位医院检验科的技师，把自己改良多年的样本处理流程写成公开文档，几家同行医院都用上了。可她科室的设备还是老几样，添置经费排在队尾。她要判断的不是自己够不够高尚，而是方法公开之后，谁来付下一轮改进的账。
paras.en: A familiar scene today: a hospital laboratory technician writes up the sample-processing method she has refined over many years as an open document, and several peer hospitals start using it. Her own department is still running the same old equipment, and the request for new purchases sits at the end of the queue. What she has to judge is not whether she is noble enough, but who pays for the next round of improvements once the method is public.

paras.zh: 另一幕在机构层面：一家小团队把整理多年的数据集免费开放，大公司拿去做成卖钱的服务，团队靠项目合同和捐助维持，做数据的人收入比跳槽低一大截。这样的组织不缺掌声，缺的是稳定经费和能留人的条件——掌声付不了房租。
paras.en: Another scene, at the level of institutions: a small team opens up a dataset it has curated for years, free of charge; large companies turn it into services that sell; the team lives on project contracts and donations, and the people who did the data work earn far less than they would by changing jobs. Organizations like that are not short of applause; they are short of stable funding and conditions that keep people around. Applause does not pay the rent.

heading.en: What This Material Cannot Tell Us

paras.zh: 边界要交代清楚：本篇的史实全部出自同一本书，1923年麦克米伦版《皮埃尔·居里》，C.与V.凯洛格英译。皮埃尔·居里传记和自传笔记都是居里夫人本人的叙述，梅洛尼那几段是她的转述，都不是独立记录。不申请专利的那个决定，书里没写日期，也没留下会议或对话的记录，本文不补写。
paras.en: The limits need to be stated. Every historical fact in this piece comes from one book: Pierre Curie, Macmillan, 1923, translated by C. and V. Kellogg. The Pierre Curie biography and the autobiographical notes are Marie Curie's own account, and the Meloney passages are her report of what she saw and heard; none of it is an independent record. The decision not to patent is undated in the book, and no minutes or conversations of the deliberations survive there; this piece does not supply them.

paras.zh: 英译在两处说法不同，本文照原文写：一处作「took no copyright」，一处作「took out no patent」。数字也照原文：十万美元、五十克、一克多、十万名妇女。她关于实干者与做梦者的那段话是她的观点，不是事实陈述；标为作者推断与作者提出的替代做法的段落，都是本文的解释，材料里没有对应记载。
paras.en: The English translation phrases the decision two different ways, and this piece follows the wording as printed: "We took no copyright" in one place, "We took out no patent" in the other. The numbers are taken as printed too: one hundred thousand dollars, fifty grammes, more than a gramme, one hundred thousand women. Her remarks about practical men and dreamers are her views, not statements of fact; the paragraphs marked as the author's inference and as the author's alternative are this piece's interpretation, with nothing in the material to match.

scenario.zh: 你和同伴花两年做出一套可申请专利、也可公开的提取方法，单位允许你们自己决定：申请保护，可能换来建实验室的钱，也可能只多一堆手续；公开，同行和客户都能立刻用上，行业可能提前起来，而你们的经费还是老样子。
scenario.en: You and a colleague spend two years developing an extraction method that could be patented or could be published. Your employer leaves the decision to you: seek protection, which might pay for a new laboratory or might only produce a pile of paperwork; or publish, so that peers and customers can use it at once, the field may get moving earlier, and your own funding stays exactly as it is.

question.zh: 动手之前，这笔账该怎么算？如果决定公开，谁该用什么机制，替公开者兜住下一轮研究的条件？
question.en: Before you start, how should the account be worked out? And if you decide to publish, who should guarantee, by what mechanism, the conditions for the next round of research by the people who published?

assumptions.zh: 假设方法确有商业价值，单位同意你们自主决定，且短期内它换不回实验室经费。
assumptions.en: Assume the method does have commercial value, that your employer genuinely lets you decide, and that in the short term it will not bring back the money for laboratory equipment.

steps.zh: 一，把收益拆成三块分别估：直接授权收入、公开后同行加速带来的合作与引用、自己研究条件的得失；二，问最坏情况：公开后若一分钱不回来，课题组还能撑多久；三，若仍选择公开，先谈好支持——单位的配套经费、设备使用权、把方法写成可交付文档的人力成本；四，把选择写成书面约定，避免事后说不清。
steps.en: First, split the returns into three parts and estimate each: direct licensing income; the collaborations and citations that come from peers accelerating once the method is public; and the gain or loss in your own research conditions. Second, ask the worst case: if not one dollar comes back after publication, how long can the group hold out? Third, if you still choose to publish, settle the support first, matching funds from your employer, access to equipment, and the person-hours needed to turn the method into a deliverable document. Fourth, put the decision in writing, so there is no dispute afterwards about what was agreed.

alternative.zh: 作者提出的替代方案（材料中没有这类讨论）：分层授权——研究与教学免费、商业使用收费；或公开方法，而把关键材料的供应留在自己手里。它能留一点收入，代价是要有人长期做谈判和监督。
alternative.en: The author's alternative, and no such discussion appears in the material: tiered licensing, free for research and teaching and paid for commercial use; or publish the method while keeping the supply of the key material in your own hands. It preserves some income, at the cost of someone doing negotiation and oversight for the long haul.

uncertainty_note.zh: 本篇事实全部来自1923年麦克米伦版《皮埃尔·居里》（C.与V.凯洛格英译）这一本书；传记与自传笔记为居里夫人自述、引言为梅洛尼转述，均非独立记录，决定的日期书中未载。
uncertainty_note.en: Every fact in this piece comes from one book, Pierre Curie (Macmillan, 1923), translated by C. and V. Kellogg: the biography and the autobiographical notes are Marie Curie's own account and the introduction is Meloney's report, none of them an independent record; the book does not date the decision.
